rows.name: Qur'an
rows.detail: Tied to the verse of debt, 2:282 ('write it down'); Ibn Abbas held this verse was revealed regarding salam.
rows.detail_long: The longest verse in the Qur'an — the debt-documentation command — is salam's anchor by Ibn Abbas's occasion-of-revelation report: advance payment for deferred delivery is a debt, and debts are to be written.

rows.name: Sahih Bukhari 2240

topics_app: Sales in which a Price is paid for Goods to be Delivered Later (As-Salam)

rows.detail: 'Whoever pays in advance, let it be for a known measure, known weight, and a fixed term' — the clearest single contract hadith of all ten.
rows.detail_long: Ibn Abbas narrates: arriving at Medina, the Prophet found people prepaying for dates a year or two out, and regulated rather than banned it. The canonical exception to 'do not sell what you do not possess.' Practiced under Abu Bakr and Umar.
rows.internal_ref: Record + grading pulled from app hadith file (kafalah_source_extract.json session)

rows.name: Jami' al-Tirmidhi 1311
rows.detail: The Madinah salam rule, dated. On arriving in Madinah the Prophet finds advance-payment for fruit already in use and regulates it: known measure, known weight, specified period.
rows.detail_long: App text read verbatim (Ibn Abbas): 'Whoever pays in advance, then let him pay in advance for known measurements, and known weights for a specified period of time.' Salam is not invented but STANDARDISED — the existing market practice is kept and given three mandatory specifications. Tirmidhi adds corroborating narrations from Ibn Abi Awfa and Abdur-Rahman bin Abza.
rows.evidence_display: Jami' al-Tirmidhi 1311 (text + grading + dating block in app)
rows.internal_ref: Record read verbatim from app hadith file (batch3_source_extract.json, 2026-07-14)

rows.timeline_year_basis: app dating block: range 622-632 (Madinan), displayed at range earliest per rule
rows.name: Bulugh al-Maram 980
rows.detail: The pre-existing practice quantified: Madinans were paying one and two YEARS in advance for fruit when the specification rule came.
rows.detail_long: App text read verbatim: 'they were paying one and two years in advance for fruits. So he said: Those who paid in advance for fruits must do so for a specified measurement and weight, and for a specified time.' The tenor of the pre-Islamic forward market — multi-year — preserved inside the regulating hadith itself.
rows.evidence_display: Bulugh al-Maram 980 (text + dating block in app)
rows.internal_ref: Record read verbatim from app hadith file (batch3_source_extract.json, 2026-07-14)

rows.timeline_year_basis: app dating block: range 622-632, displayed at range earliest per rule
rows.display_note: Companion dictum plus Malik's own doctrine in one record — fiqh forming inside the hadith corpus
rows.name: Muwatta 1397
rows.detail: Ibn Umar's salam conditions + Malik's refund rule. Ibn Umar: advance for food is fine with set description, price and date — but not in unripened crops. Malik adds: on failed delivery, take back exactly what you paid.
rows.detail_long: App text read verbatim: the companion rule (description + price + date, no advance on crops not yet ripening) and Malik's appended doctrine — if the seller cannot deliver at term and the sale is revoked, the buyer 'must only take back the silver, gold, or price which he paid exactly', and may not roll it into another purchase until repaid. The no-rollover rule protecting salam from mutating into disguised riba.
rows.internal_ref: Record read verbatim from app hadith file (batch3_source_extract.json, 2026-07-14)

rows.name: Malik ibn Anas
rows.detail: Treated as a distinct valid sale with strict conditions from Malik's Muwatta onward; all four schools follow.
rows.detail_long: From the Muwatta through al-Umm, al-Mabsut, Bada'i and al-Mughni, salam is a named contract with tight conditions — the schools differing mainly on whether goods must exist in the market between contract and delivery. App book F0778-B01.
rows.internal_ref: saa.pdf p.4; figure + book confirmed in app

rows.timeline_year_basis: adopted as rules 19-23 May 2001 (meeting 6); readopted as a Standard at meeting 8, 11-16 May 2002
rows.name: AAOIFI
rows.detail: AAOIFI Shari'ah Standard No. 10 (Salam and Parallel Salam); salam sukuk issued by Bahrain and The Gambia.
rows.detail_long: SS10 codifies salam and back-to-back parallel salam for commodity and treasury use. VERIFIED: rules adopted 23 May 2001, reformatted as Standard 16 May 2002. CLAUSES VERIFIED-TO-TEXT THIS SESSION (SS10, ss1.txt): 3/1/1 salam capital may be fungible goods provided no riba arises; 3/2/1 salam is for fungibles that can be weighed, measured or counted; 4/1 the buyer may NOT sell al-muslam fihi before taking possession; 5/1 the seller must deliver on the due date per agreed specification and quantity; 6/1 parallel salam with a third party is permitted only as a separate, independent contract.
rows.internal_ref: Verified from the official AAOIFI Shari'ah Standards 2015 full text (user-supplied PDF, adoption page read this session) | SS10 clauses read verbatim from ss1.txt (2026-07-14)

rows.name: Industry practice
rows.detail: Salam funds agriculture, trade and short-term sovereign paper (Bahrain, Gambia salam sukuk).
rows.detail_long: A niche but living structure — the pre-harvest financing tool it was in Medina, now also a treasury instrument.
